patches.title: Introducing TrueView
patches.contents: Today we're adding a new feature to demo playback called TrueView. With TrueView, demo playback will match the player's original experience much more closely.Previously, demo playback showed the server's view of the world, without accounting for network latency. patches.title: Rust director makes a public '25 million' offer to buy axed Amazon MMO New World, because "games should never die"
patches.contents: The clock on New World: Aeternum is officially ticking, with developer Amazon Games announcing that there's just one year left before its ambitious MMORPG is taken offline forever. But there's potentially a small spark of hope; Alistair McFarlane, COO and director of Rust dev Facepunch Studios, has made a public statement to Amazon Games suggesting he'd be prepared to pay '25 million' for the rights.

patches.title: After Rust's "massive" Naval update, its to-do list includes an expanded ecosystem, breeding, and maybe a battle pass
patches.contents: The Rust Naval update is just around the corner, but that's only the beginning for what could be quite a year for one of Steam's best survival games. 12 years on from launch, developer Facepunch Studios is celebrating its continued climb up the charts. 2025 saw it grow "bigger than ever," reaching a new peak player count of over 250,000 active players on Valve's platform, with more than 700 million hours played across 5.

patches.title: SURVIVING 12 YEARS
patches.contents: 12 YEARSServers are now wiped and Santa is packing up and clearing out the bodies, but we hope you enjoyed the Holiday Season. We're getting back to work after a couple of weeks off, which is why this blog is lighter than usual, but we're looking forward to the journey ahead in 2026!Last month, we celebrated Rust's 12th anniversary, marking an incredible journey. The game continues to experience year-over-year growth, which is quite remarkable for being 12 years old. Rust is now bigger than ever

patches.title: Final Round of Voting - Rust in the Steam Awards
patches.contents: We're through to the final round! But in case you're new here, over the years, Rust has undergone some huge changes - including graphic, physics, and engine updates and rebuilds, all because we’ve wanted to make Rust what it is, and what it could be. We're guided by the community, and agile enough to deliver or pivot when we need to, month after month. And this year - Rust's 12th year - we've added a new biome, new animals, new vehicles, weapons, and so much more. As well as third party collabs,

patches.title: The Rust Naval update is delayed into 2026 as Facepunch admits, "We bit off more than we could chew"
patches.contents: The Rust Naval update has been delayed into next year. "Today is not the update I wanted to ship," Facepunch Studios COO Alistair McFarlane writes at the top of a post titled, "We bit off more than we could chew." He explains that the colossal overhaul, which the developer has long been touting to arrive at the end of the year, adds a lot of new systems and touches many old ones. patches.title: Vote for Rust! The Steam Awards are now live!
patches.contents: It's that time of year again... The Steam Awards are here and the 'Labor of Love' award perfectly describes our past year as we soon hit twelve years of development! Day in and day out, our teams are grinding around the clock (literally on every continent) to keep the survival chaos alive. patches.contents: Facepunch demanded that Rust players 'Pivot or Die' with its latest update to progression changes this month, and it's not lookin' too hot for solo survivors or small groups trying to pivot. Opting out of big clans on official servers has never been the easiest way to play Rust, but recent monument, scrap, and blueprint reworks have turned the island into a real bloodbath—moreso than usual...

patches.title: New Rust update makes gunfights much riskier, so watch that trigger finger
patches.contents: A new Rust update today has rolled out a heap of the fixes for some of the survival game's longest-running frustrations and foibles. Developer Facepunch Studios has been deploying some hefty overhauls in recent months, but for September it's taken a slight step back from piling in new features to steady the ship and refine on what's already there. The Rust Maintenance update is "focused on tackling a number of long-standing bugs and improvements" based on community feedback.

We’ve been working through community feedback to smooth out some of the more persistent issues and make everyday gameplay feel that bit better. patches.title: Dead by Daylight dev is hiring for people with generative AI experience
patches.contents: September 18, 2025 - Responding to a request for comment, Behaviour Interactive tells PCGamesN: "We have a very firm policy that prevents the inclusion of anything generated by AI in Dead by Daylight or any other game we're working on, including marketing assets. Yes, Behaviour is exploring the use of generative AI tools to improve internal workflows; not for anything that ships in our games. Our policy isn't changing, and these job offerings are not for roles on any game team."

patches.title: Dead By Daylight dev apologizes to angry fans and promises Kill Switch overhaul
patches.contents: It's been a particularly tricky few days for Dead By Daylight - a game that is, admittedly, no stranger to bumps in the road. A couple of buggy patches and problematic perks, and criticism of Behaviour Interactive's Kill Switch system, has seen community sentiment sour despite the recent release of its The Walking Dead crossover. Now, Behaviour has issued a statement apologizing to DBD fans for the recent issues and promising a review and overhaul of the Kill Switch.

patches.title: Bug Fix Status Update + 9.1.1 Patch Notes
patches.contents: Hello folks, We have followed your conversations very closely about the state of the game of late, and we agree it’s not in the place we all would like it to be. Recent releases, including our most recent, have introduced frustrating new issues which have distracted from your enjoyment of DbD. patches.title: Space Marine 2 dev says "no one is abandoning the game" in favor of the sequel
patches.contents: Warhammer 40k Space Marine 2 might be getting a sequel, but developer Saber Interactive is keen to reassure players that the current iteration isn't going away any time soon. "We're excited to see your enthusiasm," the studio writes about the recent Space Marine 3 announcement, "although we hear those of you who fear for Space Marine 2 and its future support." As its first round of PTS testing rolls on, the developer outlines what's still ahead for SM2.

patches.title: Space Marine 2 PTS lets you test the next update's Inferno Pistol right now
patches.contents: The Warhammer 40k Space Marine 2 PTS has arrived, and you can get an early look at some of the big beats of patch 7.0 right now. The new public test server lets anyone dive in and try the next Space Marine 2 update either solo or in multiplayer. To start with, Saber Interactive is trialling its upcoming overhaul, which includes a new PvE map, adjustments to weapon restrictions and perks, PvP matchmaking improvements, and a new secondary weapon, the iconic 40k Inferno Pistol.

patches.contents: Space Marine 2 has already cemented itself as one of the biggest Warhammer videogames ever, but the co-op shooter is keen to keep on evolving, improving, and expanding. patches.contents: Another day, another Baldur's Gate 3 hotfix, this one being number 34, or version 4.1.1.6931813 of the game if you really want to be specific. There's a number of fixes we'll get to in a minute, but first the thing you're probably most excited to hear: it has a native Steam Deck build now! Developer Larian Studios shared word of this change in a Steam news post today, and what exactly it means for you.

patches.title: Ex Dragon Age writer fears publishers will learn "the wrong lessons" from BG3
patches.contents: It's no secret that Baldur's Gate 3 is among the greatest RPGs ever made. From its sprawling, living world to its cast of lovable yet complex characters, Larian's Dungeons and Dragons epic rightfully deserves its place in the spotlight. In its wake, we've seen a resurgence in narrative-driven RPGs, with Sandfall's Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 being the latest triumph. But with BG3 now being considered the gold standard for RPGs, others will, of course, try to emulate its success.

patches.contents: The Diablo 4 Berserk crossover has arrived in Sanctuary, but it proves a rather expensive outing if you're looking to dress up for the occasion. patches.contents: A new Diablo 4 hotfix is here, as Blizzard dramatically adjusts the reputation gains on offer in its latest update. patches.contents: Season 8: Belial’s Return has officially kicked off in Diablo 4, and it has not been off to the best of starts. Usually, the gameplay implications of all the design and balance changes take a little while to bubble up to the surface - at least as far as the wider player base is concerned.

patches.contents: Diablo 4 Season 8 is a significant one for a variety of reasons, but one of the biggest is the introduction of Reliquaries, which replace its old battle pass system. With D4's challenge set to ramp up as Belial, the Lord of Lies, returns as the new pinnacle encounter, I'm certainly pleased to hear that I'll be getting bonuses sooner in Season 8.

We’ve known much about Season 8: Belial’s Return thanks to the PTR (Public Test Realm) the developer hosted for the new season last month, and quite unsurprisingly, not much has changed.

patches.contents: As Diablo 4 struggles to find its feet despite stellar launch reviews and an equally brilliant expansion, former Blizzard president Mike Ybarra has taken to X (formerly Twitter) to explain how he'd fix the game's issues. patches.contents: For Diablo 4 players, the news that there wouldn't be a new expansion this year was a pretty tough pill to swallow. However, with the reveal of its roadmap for 2025 and beyond, Blizzard may have just sweetened the deal. Confirming the themes of the RPG's next three seasons and some of the major content they contain, it also teases that the heavily requested leaderboards feature will be arriving - albeit not until next year.

patches.contents: Blizzard has revealed the patch notes for Diablo 4’s next update, which will arrive tomorrow, March 18 on all platforms. This is a smaller patch, so don’t expect anything massive. Ironically, though, the biggest change has little to do with gameplay. Read more

patches.contents: One of the foremost faces of the Diablo 4 development team is stepping down from Blizzard after 15 years at the studio. patches.contents: The PA-28-236 Dakota: Refined and ResilientWhen first delivered in 1979, the Piper PA-28-236 Dakota represented a refined evolution of a Piper aircraft family that dated back nearly two decades. patches.contents: REPO has spent the last few weeks growing on Steam, and now it's one of the biggest games on Valve's platform. The spooky indie is so big, in fact, that it just beat out the likes of GTA 5 Enhanced and Stardew Valley, as players band together to make some cash in the Lethal Company-style online experience. patches.contents: I'm going to have to upgrade to Windows 11. That much is now inevitable, and not just to ensure my own peace of mind as Microsoft ends security upgrades. While you might still be able to play, the developer warns that it will no longer provide support for any problems that arise as a result.

patches.title: Final Fantasy 14 Mobile is live now, but not for everyone
patches.contents: Ever since Square Enix announced Final Fantasy 14 Mobile, I've been hungrily waiting for the chance to try it. It's the MMORPG that made me fall in love with the entire genre, so the prospect of playing it on the go is something I can wholeheartedly get behind. The bad news is FF14 Mobile is coming to China first, with the Western release on the way soon after. The good news, though, is that it finally launched in China, meaning we hopefully don't have long to wait.

patches.contents: The FF14 7.2 release date is confirmed, as game director Naoki Yoshida and community producer Toshio Murouchi come together once more to show us what the next Dawntrail patch looks like. The new update for Square Enix's critically acclaimed MMORPG is a big one, and looks to deliver the long-form content that players have been asking for. In today's FF14 Live Letter 86, the pair dive in to give us a closer look at everything coming in patch 7.2.

patches.title: FF14 director Yoshida squashes rumors about his executive status at Square Enix
patches.contents: As he shows off the new FF14 update, game director 'Yoshi-P' has put to bed swirling rumors about his status on the board at Square Enix. A post noting that Yoshida had not been mentioned in the company's yearly reports recently led to some speculation that he would no longer continue as an executive. During the pre-show for FF14 Live Letter 86, however, he confirms that these rumors are inaccurate.

patches.title: FF14 warns of potential bans as it changes its policy on fraudulent game time
patches.contents: Square Enix is telling Final Fantasy 14 players it will start suspending their accounts if they have redeemed fraudulent game time cards, as it changes its policy on giving users the "benefit of the doubt." Going forward, FF14 subscribers who have purposefully or accidentally added crooked game time to their account may need to pay Square Enix the retail value of the transaction to get their Warrior of Light back.

patches.contents: Despite sitting alongside the big guns in our best survival games list, Icarus is a beautiful yet strange anomaly. As is always the way when dealing with Group 15, you may find you leave with more questions than answers. What has Mo been doing since your discovery on Prometheus? patches.title: Icarus Week 167 Update | Achievement Fixes, Sleep Screen improvements, and more
patches.contents: Welcome to Week 167. This week, we have a number of smaller fixes and some QoL. We have highlighted some below, but check out the patch notes for the full list. We go into detail about the Achievement Fixes and Changes and a new addition to the sleep screen. Finally, we discuss a feature that has been requested for a long time—tree regrowth—which, if all goes well, will be released next week. patches.title: Icarus Week 166 Update | World Boss Exotics, Double XP & Extra Talent Points
patches.contents: Welcome to Week 166. We’re kicking off a Double XP weekend, a great chance to earn those talent and blueprint points that have been evading you. World Bosses have also been given a valuable update, with lootable resources that include exotics. We have also converted two existing missions so that on completion you will earn additional talent points for your characters. Jump in and have a read. {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38036764/0d3db0430ae3bb04db9fa9bb39c5fb36be36819b.png Notable Improvements: Fix Seed

patches.title: Icarus Week 165 Update | Hammerhead Slug World Boss
patches.contents: Welcome to Week 165. Today, the Hammerhead Slug World Boss is introduced to the swamps of Icarus. We also give a sneak peek into what is coming next week, allowing all bosses to be lootable when killed and a quality pass on their rewards. If you want to fight the Hammerhead Slug, you will need to play on the Prometheus Map in the New Frontiers Expansion. It can be purchased here: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1648532/Icarus_New_Frontiers_Expansion/ Notable Improvements: Added additional Bla

patches.title: Hotfix Version: 2.2.39.132295
patches.contents: Contains the Following Fixes: Fix invisible materials for various assets including the Fishing Bench and Creature Deterrent

patches.title: Icarus Week 164 Update | Lava Hunter World Boss Spawning
patches.contents: Welcome to Week 164. This week, we’ve enabled the Lava Hunter World Boss on Prometheus to spawn outside of its specific mission. This will allow you to fight it over and over again without having to start new prospects. We’ve also done a quality-of-life pass on the rest of the world bosses' spawns to address their regularity so you can engage them more. Jump in and have a read. patches.title: Hotfix Version: 2.2.38.131942
patches.contents: Contains the Following Fixes: Fixed issue where radars and scanners couldn't be activated which could block both exotic scanning and various mission progress.

patches.title: Icarus Week 163 Update | New Year Bug Fixes & QoL Improvements
patches.contents: Welcome to Week 163. This week's theme is bug fixes and QoL. Thanks to feedback over the holiday period, we have addressed a number of issues. We have also fixed an issue that was limiting client performance. We also have some details on what is to come next week involving the Lava Hunter present on Prometheus. Jump in and have a read. Notable Improvements: Coconut Trees grown in crop plots now provide Wood when harvested C0NT4CT Radio will now find the most upgraded C0NT4CT device to connect to

patches.title: The latest Peak update does in fact see the forest for the trees with its fungus and bug-filled woods
patches.contents: There is perhaps no better setting than some woods or a forest that just sucks ass. Just a confusing, scary, maybe sometimes enchanting mess of nature that is impossible to navigate. Today's latest update for Peak just so happens to present such a visage, with towering, beautiful trees, and yet again a wonderful sense of scale.

patches.title: 1.31 - Achievement fix, PvP scoring improvements and more
patches.contents: Hi everyone, another bug fix patch coming in.We did some investigating about the black screen issue some people have, especially when their ping is high (over 100). It turns out it's related to the amount of items the host has in his hideout - each item has physics, and if there's too many of these items and the connection isn't great, clients may not sync properly and the black screen happens.The fix - for now - would be to limit items in the hideout to 100, but only for people with bad connect

patches.contents: So the Steam Awards are here… and I honestly had no idea what to choose. On one hand, it’s that game that makes you clench your teeth because you know you can beat this job, but somehow everything still goes sideways. patches.contents: Once upon a time, when I was a bright-eyed, bushy-tailed university student, I wrote a dissertation on L.A. Noire. While my main focus was its portrayal of PTSD in 1940s America, it's the ending that sticks with me most. I, like many, found protagonist Cole Phelps to be thoroughly unlikable, even arrogant, yet the conclusion of his story still hits hard because he's so convincingly written. patches.title: A Global Campaign | Feature Focus
patches.contents: Welcome to Module 5 of the Dinosaur Integration Network training series. In this module we’ll be taking a closer look at the work you’ll be doing with DIN across the globe – building and rebuilding parks, unlocking new locations, dinosaurs and more. As Park Manager, you'll need to balance the competing priorities of Security, Entertainment, and Conservation. Your decisions will shape your campaign, earning rewards like new technologies but be prepared, not everyone will support your vision.

patches.title: Feature Focus | Building Your Parks
patches.contents: Welcome to the fourth Dinosaur Integration Network training video. Today’s episode takes a closer look at the modular scenery customisation and how park managers can tweak every aspect of their parks from the ground up.

patches.title: Dinosaur Showcase | Utahraptor
patches.contents: Meet the Utahraptor — one of the largest and most formidable dromaeosaurs available for your parks in Jurassic World Evolution 3. patches.title: Captain's Diary #50: Post-launch payload
patches.contents: Hi everyone, Captain Marek here with our 50th diary post. It’s been four weeks since Update 3 dropped, and we’ve already shipped five major patches that add new content, polish the UI/UX, and squash lots of bugs. Let’s take a look at how the launch went, what’s new since then, and what’s coming next!Update 3 launch recap & highlightsUpdate 3 landed with a bang! We shattered our previous record of 6.1k concurrent players (set back in 2022) on every weekend since release, peaking at 11121 players!

patches.title: How to make Ghostly Fish Steak in Disney Dreamlight Valley
patches.contents: Ghostly Fish Steak is one of the more peculiar recipes you'll eventually learn in Disney Dreamlight Valley , and surprisingly, it's not one locked behind a DLC. It's a five-star entree, so it can be a valuable meal to make on a whim to boost your energy. Or, even to make some quick cash if you've been eyeing up an upgrade you can't quite afford. But its ingredients aren't as easy to gather as your standard meal.

patches.title: How to make Biryani in Disney Dreamlight Valley
patches.contents: Biryani is a five-star dish in Disney Dreamlight Valley, so it's a valuable recipe to learn if you're constantly spending your days rinsing through your energy bar and need a quick boost. Because of its high quality, you'll need five ingredients to make it, and some of these are locked behind the Rift in Time DLC, so you won't be able to collect what you need solely from the valley...

patches.title: How to make a Spiral Strawberry Smoothie in Disney Dreamlight Valley
patches.contents: If you want to know how to make a Spiral Strawberry Smoothie in Disney Dreamlight Valley, then you'll be happy to know it's not a difficult recipe to master at all. You'll need two ingredients that are easy to come by, but the only catch is they are exclusive to The Storybook Vale DLC...
